title.title: Every log canonical MMP on a fourfold terminates
title.subtitle: Claim: every sequence of log canonical flips on a projective fourfold stops, with Kähler analogues

plain: A step-by-step simplification of 4D shapes can never run forever: every chain of moves stops

object.caption: each step is a flip $X_i \dashrightarrow X_{i+1}$ (schematic)

beats.text: The minimal model program improves a variety one flip at a time
Termination: no chain of flips can go on forever
Claimed for log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary

achievement.label: Termination of flips in dimension 4
achievement.context: Before: terminal and canonical fourfolds (Shokurov 2004), klt with scaling (Alexeev–Hacon–Kawamata 2007)
achievement.note: The Kähler results cover existing flip sequences only

verify.detail: No Lean; 231 pages, and two manuscripts share one title
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: The minimal model program simplifies a variety by a sequence of flips.
Must every sequence stop? Open past dimension three.
Claimed: every log canonical sequence of flips stops on fourfolds.

sources.ref: article, Termination of flips on fourfolds (family 056)
